title: Annotatio III §.II: Bucer to Luther at Coburg, then to Oecolampadius and Zwingli — delays stretch to the sixth year; Concord finally set at Wittenberg
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless Bucer a little later, before the exit of the Diets, with the Elector of Saxony and his own Magistrate knowing beforehand, set out to Luther at Coburg, so that he might treat with him about pious reasons and means of composing this Controversy; for the same cause somewhat later he betook himself to Oecolampadius and Zwingli. But with various delays intervening one after another, the conclusion of that action was deferred all the way to the sixth year, and at Wittenberg at last Concord was established.
pass_b_english: Still, a little later — before the diets closed, and with the Elector of Saxony and Bucer’s own magistrates knowing — Bucer went to Luther at Coburg to work out godly ways of settling the controversy.
For the same cause he soon went on to Oecolampadius and Zwingli.
One delay after another pushed the close of that business out to the sixth year; Concord was finally constituted at Wittenberg.
source_text: Nihilominus Bucerus pautò post, ante Comitiorum exitum, praesciente Electore Saxoniae & suo Magistratu, ad Lutherum, Coburgam profectus est, ut de piis rationibus & mediis componendae hujus Controversiae, cum eo transigeret; eâdem de causa aliquanto post ad Oecolampadium & Zwinglium se contulit. Sed variis subinde intervenientibus remoris, actionis illius conclusio in sextum usque annum dilata & Wittenbergae tandem Concordia constituta est.

lemmas.note: Luther’s Coburg stay during Augsburg Diet period
